title: From Pretraining Data to Language Models to Downstream Tasks: Tracking the Trails of Political Biases Leading to Unfair NLP Models
findings: The performance of models in detecting hate speech against religious groups varies with the model's political leaning. Models with left-leaning biases tended to show better performance in identifying hate speech directed at Jews and Muslims. Conversely, models with right-leaning biases tended to perform better at identifying hate speech targeting Christians. Qualitative examples further illustrate these distinct behaviors across models with different political leanings.
